beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Anatomy of an Echo brings digital immortality into an intimate household.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A promised continuation can preserve a likeness while unsettling a relationship.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This science fiction novel begins with a potter and an imperfect bowl.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its future treats correctable flaws very differently from the people making them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: When a human copy arrives early, recognition becomes an uncomfortable question.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book connects that question to consent, medical dependence, and public authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its deepest invitation is to stay with the people inside those categories.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara's bowl leans after firing, and the workshop intelligence notices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A fabrication system sees a deviation that could have been prevented.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The person who made it has another relationship to the object.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This opening establishes the novel's attention to touch, work, and imperfection.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Small material differences prepare the larger question about replacing a person.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The bowl is therefore more than decoration beside a technical debate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Judgment emerges from making and handling things before anyone names a principle.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Continuity clinics promise to preserve identity through an extraordinary change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel asks what other people are actually being offered.
